Usage: memoriahub backup restore [options]

Restore a backup root back into a MemoriaHub server

Options:
  --root <dir>            Backup root to restore FROM (the folder `backup init
                          --dest` created)
  --dry-run               Print the full plan (circle mapping + totals) and
                          write nothing
  --into-circle <id>      Restore every source circle into this existing circle
  --map-circle <src=dst>  Map one source circle id to a target circle id
                          (repeatable)
  --include <what>        Extra scope: "trashed" (restored as ACTIVE items).
                          Repeatable.
  --concurrency <n>       Concurrent upload workers (default: 2)
  --skip-metadata         Upload originals only — reapply no sidecar metadata
  --json                  Emit NDJSON events instead of human output
  -h, --help              display help for command

AUTHENTICATION
  Restore writes media, albums, tags and people, so it needs a NORMAL account
  login (`memoriahub login`) or a personal access token. A `nod_` node
  credential is refused up front: the server accepts it ONLY on /api/nodes/*
  routes, so it can never reach any endpoint a restore needs.

CIRCLE MAPPING (precedence)
  1. --map-circle <sourceCircleId>=<targetCircleId>
  2. --into-circle <targetCircleId>  (everything lands there)
  3. find-or-create a circle matching the sidecar's circle name
  The resolved mapping is printed before anything is written; an unknown
  --map-circle/--into-circle target is a hard error BEFORE the first write.

SCOPE
  Default: every `present` item — active AND archived (archived items are
  restored, then re-archived at the end). --include trashed additionally
  restores trashed rows, but they land as ACTIVE items: no public API can
  put an item back into the server's Trash. Quarantined items are NEVER
  restored — the server no longer lists them.

WHAT IS NOT RESTORED
  Detected faces (bounding boxes / embeddings), thumbnails, EXIF-derived
  columns, perceptual hashes and burst/duplicate grouping are DERIVED data:
  enrichment regenerates them from the restored bytes. People associations
  ARE restored, by name.

RE-RUNNABLE
  Every restored item records the MediaItem id it landed on. A second run
  verifies those ids and skips them; anything else is caught by server-side
  content-hash dedup. Interrupt it freely and re-run.
